rationale: Repair of trial-1a25041f29 (rejected: paired_gain_not_above_noise, gains 1.99/2.95 ms vs MAD bounds 1.26/5.66 ms). The previous trial's own quality telemetry shows why the gain was only ~2-3 ms: every prefill invocation ran the route 'parent-eager' (count 2), i.e. the fused composite and its CUDA graph never executed; its build-time verification had returned False at candidate.py:338 (hidden-state allclose). Root cause, diagnosed on CPU with the actual asset weights in the measured worker environment (transformers 5.16.1, inspected with /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python): Qwen3RMSNorm returns weight * round_bf16(x_norm_fp32) - the round to bf16 happens BEFORE the weight multiply - while the previous fused q/k kernel computed round_bf16(x_norm_fp32 * weight_fp32) with a single rounding. Qwen3-4B q/k norm weights reach 44.0, so the missing intermediate rounding produced up to 2.0 absolute error on layer-0 keys (reproduced: norm-vs-parent maxdiff 2.0, rope exact 0.0), drifted last_hidden_state by ~1.0 through 36 layers and failed verification, silently degrading to parent-eager. This candidate keeps the parent's exact per-op rounding sequence everywhere: round-then-weight q/k RMSNorm, bf16 RoPE arithmetic with the parent's per-op rounding order (cos/sin halves from the parent's own rotary module, already bf16), ATen-form SiLU x/(1+exp(-x)) in fp32 rounded once then bf16 multiply, ATen-form mean (sum * float(1/N)) and rsqrt in the fused kernels, the parent's own GEMM shapes/weights (no qkv/gate-up consolidation, so every cuBLAS call matches the parent bit-for-bit), the same SDPA flash call (attn_mask=None, is_causal=True, scale=head_dim**-0.5, enable_gqa=True) on identically strided contiguous [B,H,S,D] q/k/v, and KV cache entries written directly in the parent's post-rope contiguous layout (replacing DynamicCache's empty-cat copies at prefill). The stack is fused into three Triton kernels (add+RMSNorm with residual round, per-head q/k-norm+RoPE+transpose, SiLU*up) plus the unchanged GEMMs/SDPA (~500 kernels vs 2146, eliminating the ~1456-launch eager elementwise tail and all prefill cat kernels), and the verified composite is captured once into a CUDA graph at installation; every invocation copies the current input_ids into the static buffer and replays, removing the ~3.3 ms of exposed host dispatch (measured: clean ttft 24.611 ms vs 21.34 ms GPU busy in observations/current/nsys-9ed9145c.json). CPU validation on the real weights at the observed signature [1,256]: last_hidden_state, all 36 cached keys and values bitwise equal to the parent (maxdiff 0), and three greedy decode steps through the wrapped DynamicCache view reproduce the parent chain exactly (hidden diff 0.0, equal tokens, cache length 256->259), so decode-side torch.cat growth, continuous execution and reset semantics are preserved. The decode call e7df98b905ed8aa688d5227a passes through the live parent reference unchanged (31 calls/run), preserving cache growth and the secondary decode goal. Installation verifies the eager composite and a graph replay against the live parent reference on two fresh random token-id tensors with tight per-tensor thresholds (hidden<=0.10, k<=1.20 with mean<=2e-3, v<=0.10 with mean<=1e-3; the failing previous version measured hidden 1.0 / k 2.0, expected residual ulp noise is far below) and walks a fallback ladder composite-graph -> eager-composite -> parent-graph (captured from the raw module forward, not the binding wrapper) -> parent-eager, each transition reported as a distinct route label (setup-failure:composite-verify / graph-capture-composite / graph-verify / graph-capture-parent, parent-fallback-signature, runtime-failure:parent-fallback), so quality execution telemetry will show which path actually ran; expected quality route is 'graph-replay:composite' count 2 and 'parent-passthrough' count 62. No inner call's compute is eliminated: the prefill children execute as native kernels inside the graph rather than as separately dispatched eager calls, and the boundary returns the parent's BaseModelOutputWithPast structure (fresh DynamicCache per invocation), so every consumer (lm_head slice, adapter argmax, decode cache) remains valid; no other bundle is installed (search.json installed_bundles empty). Measured opportunity (not a claim): 16.91 ms GEMM near roofline + ~0.7 ms attention + ~4.4 ms non-GEMM elementwise (fused to ~1-1.5 ms) + ~3.3 ms exposed dispatch gives a testable target of ~19-21 ms ttft and paired gains of roughly 5.5-8 ms against the observed same-worker parents (26.26/27.56), above both noise bounds - a hypothesis the paired revalidation must confirm; if the fused graph path does not engage, the route labels will expose that immediately rather than publishing a parent-eager run as before.

setup_work.when: installation (build), outside the measured invocation; no adapter phase context is entered and no fixture input is used - verification runs on freshly drawn random token ids each installation
steps: Read batch/prompt length from the observed prefill signature in context targets (fallback: state workload) and take the module, weights and live parent reference from context modules/references.
Compute rotary cos/sin half-tables once for positions 0..S-1 with the parent's own rotary module (position-only, input-value independent; ~64 KB bf16 kept resident).
JIT-compile and probe the three Triton kernels on tiny dummies; on any Triton failure fall back to the bitwise-exact pure-torch ops (route: setup-failure:triton-unavailable).

Verify the eager composite against the live parent reference on two random inputs: last_hidden_state plus all 36 layers' cached keys/values, with tight per-tensor thresholds (hidden<=0.10, k<=1.20/mean 2e-3, v<=0.10/mean 1e-3) and per-tensor diagnostic route labels on failure.

Side-stream warmup (2 runs) then one CUDA graph capture of the verified composite on a static input buffer; verify graph replay on the same two random inputs against the parent with the same thresholds; on failure use the eager composite (still fused kernels) or, if the composite itself failed verification, capture the raw module forward as a parent graph verified to <=0.02, else parent-eager.
Final torch.cuda.synchronize; no torch.cuda.empty_cache and no weight mutation.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates the rotary half-tables (~64 KB), static input_ids (2 KB) and one CUDA graph with its private memory pool holding one prefill forward's static outputs/intermediates (order a few hundred MB, retained for replay). Because activation allocation moves into the graph pool, warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes can fall while framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes rises; this is pool accounting, not a claim of physical-memory savings. Build cost is dominated by Triton JIT compilation and ~6 verification forwards (well inside the 900 s worker timeout; the previous trial's full ladder measured 1.6 s without JIT).

quality_risks: Triton tl.sum reduction order differs from ATen's mean, so a few elements per forward may flip by one bf16 ulp (fp32 variance last-ulp crossing, amplified by q/k norm weights up to 44 to <=1.0 on rare key elements); build-time verification bounds this (hidden<=0.10 vs parent) and CPU validation shows the op-level formulas are bitwise exact, but GPU reduction-order residue cannot be CPU-proven - thresholds and the fallback ladder are the guard.

require_exact_greedy_tokens: greedy tokens are argmax over bf16 logits; if two logits were within ~1e-3 the residual ulp drift could flip a token. The previous trial passed the same discrete gate, and expected logit drift here is far below the observed top-1 margins, but this remains a distribution-level risk mitigated only by the verification thresholds.

CUDA graph replay reuses static output buffers; each invocation rewrites them. Sequential single-stream execution (prefill -> 31 decode steps -> reset/sync) means no live consumer can observe a stale or overwritten buffer, and the wrapper returns a fresh DynamicCache per invocation; continuous_steps=2 was validated on CPU at the cache level (bitwise decode continuity).

Graph capture could fail on the worker (cuBLAS workspace, Triton capture, flash kernel); the ladder then runs the eager composite or a verified parent graph, trading speed for preserved quality, and the route label discloses it - no silent parent-eager publication as in the previous trial.
Decode passes through the parent untouched, so cache growth and the secondary decode_tokens_per_second goal are unchanged by construction.
